scope: AnalyticsPrivacyTests.swift fixture/path correction, three fixture regressions and one queued-retry regression; 18 authored methods. Production source unchanged.
source_resolution_assessment: The retry test asserts the exact expected endpoint URL and responds 404. The deprecated URL.path trailing-slash comparison and silent unmatched-route branch are removed.
Each session has a fresh UUID additional-header scope, and handlers are keyed by scope. Separate HTTP-status-loop sessions no longer overwrite one process-global current handler.

makeTransport tracks every test transport. Teardown revokes them, invalidates/cancels all sessions, waits for each invalidation delegate at the unchanged two-second bound, then removes only those scope registrations. URLSession retains its delegate; immutable expectation references are fulfilled from delegate callbacks.

Protocol instances capture their stop handler. waiting/loading/stopped/finished state makes repeated stop and late response inert. The recursive state lock permits inline respond from the start callback; the global registry lock is released before callbacks.

The configured protocol still accepts requests before resolving the scope. Missing or retired scopes fail through URLProtocolClient with a cancelled error rather than falling through to real HTTP or another session's handler.

The URLProtocolClient spy covers required redirect/cache/response/data/finish/fail/challenge selectors, with locked counters. No high-confidence API, Swift closure or delegate-signature defect was identified by inspection; actual SDK typecheck remains required.

Three direct protocol regressions cover held-A/configured-B stop ownership, retired-scope fail-closed behavior and one-shot cancellation. They do not themselves exercise actual URLSession header augmentation/invalidation.

The fourth new test obtains a valid enabled lease, queues work with 0.1-second delay, revokes consent and retains the 0.3-second inverted wait. It covers work queued before revocation, distinct from scheduling an already-revoked lease. This transport-level regression does not establish that the reporter test had already scheduled its own retry.

independent_checks.check: Production transport/telemetry hashes match frozen triage
Complete changed test file, lifecycle, fixture regressions and final queued-retry test reviewed

remaining_native_acceptance: Compile against the actual Xcode SDK and run all 18 privacy tests before the full app gate. No native execution was performed by this Windows reviewer.

Confirm additional-header scope is present on actual custom-protocol requests and invalidation delegate fires once within the existing two-second cleanup bound. Apple documents session-task header augmentation, but that integration is unexecuted here.

Retain original timing, callback, cancellation and overfulfillment checks. Verify all six previous failures in a fresh process, repeat the full class serially, then obtain a full app/smoke pass without crash or restart.

For any remaining timeout, collect identity-bound start/respond/session-completion/telemetry-callback checkpoints before changing production or timeout bounds. The fixture correction does not prove every original timeout had the same cause.
nonblocking_limits: Reporter retry test fulfills first before the 404 completion schedules its retry; main may revoke before a reporter retry exists. It proves no subsequent request after revocation, with the separate transport test covering queued-before-revoke work. A deterministic reporter scheduling barrier remains additional coverage.

Session invalidation drains URLSession callbacks; telemetry acknowledgments dispatched later to a global queue are separate work. They now retain their own scopes/expectations, but failed test callbacks still need trace evidence when diagnosing persistent timeouts.
Approval is source/test architecture review, not native compilation, runtime success or release certification.
mutations: Only this review receipt was written; no implementation edits, prior receipt changes, commit or push.
